Software Development Lifecycle.text: Which SDLC model emphasizes iterative development with frequent client feedback?
Software Development Lifecycle.explanation: Agile uses short iterations and frequent stakeholder feedback to refine requirements.

Software Development Lifecycle.text: What is the main deliverable of the Requirements Analysis phase?
Software Development Lifecycle.explanation: The Requirements Spec Document captures all functional and non-functional requirements.

Software Development Lifecycle.text: In the Waterfall model, which phase comes immediately after Design?
Software Development Lifecycle.explanation: After design, the implementation (coding) phase builds the software.

Software Development Lifecycle.text: Which lifecycle model allows returning to previous phases at any time?
Software Development Lifecycle.explanation: Iterative models let you revisit and refine earlier phases continuously.

Software Development Lifecycle.text: What is the purpose of the Maintenance phase?
Software Development Lifecycle.explanation: Maintenance fixes bugs and improves the system after deployment.
RAD focuses on rapidly building prototypes to gather early feedback.

Software Development Lifecycle.text: The V-Model maps testing activities to:
Software Development Lifecycle.explanation: In the V-Model, each dev phase has a corresponding testing phase.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: Which principle hides the internal state of an object?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: Encapsulation restricts direct access to object data.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: Which concept refers to one interface, multiple implementations?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: Polymorphism lets different classes respond to the same method call.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: What allows a class to derive properties from another?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: Inheritance lets a subclass inherit methods and fields from its parent.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: Which OOP concept represents a real-world entity?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: A class is a blueprint for objects modelling real entities.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: What keyword in many languages creates a subclass?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: `extends` (Java, etc.) signals that one class inherits another.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: Which keyword calls the parent class constructor?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: `super()` invokes the parent’s constructor in many OOP languages.

Object-Oriented Programming.text: What pattern restricts object instantiation to one instance?
Object-Oriented Programming.explanation: The Singleton pattern ensures only one instance of a class exists.

Algorithms.text: What’s the time complexity of binary search on a sorted array?
Algorithms.explanation: Binary search halves the search range each step: O(log n).

Algorithms.text: Which algorithm finds the shortest path in a weighted graph?
Algorithms.explanation: Dijkstra’s algorithm computes shortest paths with non-negative weights.

Algorithms.text: Quick sort’s average case time complexity is:
Algorithms.explanation: On average, quick sort runs in O(n log n) time.

Algorithms.text: Which sort is stable and uses additional memory proportional to n?
Algorithms.explanation: Merge sort is stable and needs O(n) extra space.

Algorithms.text: Which search algorithm uses a queue?
Algorithms.explanation: BFS uses a queue to explore neighbor nodes level by level.
Negative weights break Dijkstra’s correctness, so weights ≥0 are required.
Greedy methods pick the best immediate choice, not necessarily global best.

Data Structures.explanation: Queues dequeue in the order items were enqueued.

Data Structures.text: A balanced binary search tree ensures:
Data Structures.explanation: Balance keeps depth ~log n, so operations are O(log n).

Data Structures.text: What is a hash table’s average lookup time?
Data Structures.explanation: With a good hash, average lookup is constant time O(1).

Data Structures.text: Linked list where each node has two references is called:
Data Structures.explanation: Doubly linked lists have `prev` and `next` pointers per node.

Data Structures.text: Which structure best models hierarchical data?
A Bloom filter may yield false positives.
Data Structures.explanation: Bloom filters can say 'present' erroneously but never 'absent' falsely.

Databases.text: Which normal form removes transitive dependencies?
Databases.explanation: 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies between non-key fields.

Databases.text: In ACID properties, what does “I” stand for?
Databases.explanation: I is Isolation: transactions should not interfere with each other.

Databases.text: Which SQL command removes a row?
A JOIN that returns all rows from the left table is:
Databases.explanation: LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the left table, matching or not.
MongoDB is a document-oriented NoSQL database.
Indexes speed up searches at the cost of some extra storage.

Operating Systems.text: Which OS concept manages multiple processes?
Operating Systems.explanation: Process Scheduling controls which process runs when.
Virtual memory combines RAM and disk to extend address space.

Operating Systems.text: A race condition is a type of:
Operating Systems.explanation: Race conditions occur when processes interleave unpredictably.
It allocates fixed time slices to each process in turn.

Operating Systems.text: In OS, a semaphore is used for:
Operating Systems.explanation: Semaphores coordinate access to shared resources.
Thrashing is excessive page swapping, degrading performance.

Operating Systems.text: Kernel mode vs user mode: the kernel has:
Operating Systems.explanation: Kernel mode code runs with full hardware privileges.

Software Testing.explanation: Unit tests verify small code units (e.g., functions) in isolation.
Integration tests check interactions between modules.
Coverage shows which parts of code were executed by tests.
Mocks stand in for real dependencies to isolate units under test.
It ensures that older functionality still works after changes.
Black-box tests treat the system as a “closed box,” checking outputs.
Load tests check how well a system handles high user/concurrent load.

Agile Methodologies.explanation: Scrum organizes work into fixed-length sprints.

Agile Methodologies.text: In Scrum, who prioritizes the backlog?
Agile Methodologies.explanation: The Product Owner orders the Product Backlog items.
Kanban focuses on continuous delivery and limiting WIP.

Agile Methodologies.text: A user story template often starts with:
Agile Methodologies.explanation: Full template: “As a <role>, I want <goal> so that <benefit>.”
Stand-ups are time-boxed to about 15 minutes.
Velocity is the amount of story points completed each sprint.
Retrospectives happen after each sprint to reflect and improve.
